title: Map 2: size of gain against matched share
description: Test 6's setup: matched and unmatched workers produce 1 in the sector and in X; the young curve; the sector at 0.1% of spending. Matched workers' output rises by 1 + g. η is the number of matched people as a multiple of the sector's base-year employment. Outcomes: the price, matched workers' pay relative to X, and the regime. Hand-worked boundaries: matched workers are scarce while η (1 + g) ≤ 1, and plentiful once η (1 + g) > Q(1/(1 + g)). The regime is read from who works in the sector (explain.ts): scarce while unmatched workers still make at least 1% of its units, plentiful once matched workers earn within 5% of their X pay. Those are conventions for large θ: at low θ some unmatched workers always stay, so cells read as scarce even where the price has fallen.

outcomes.label: Matched workers’ pay premium over X
